input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed against input/disclosure.md and the affirmative USER passages in input/conversation.md (the single technical USER passage being the autonomous-mode message: "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"), with input/brief.md used only for title, applicant/inventor, priority and government-support formalities. A complete ledger was built and traced item by item. All 20 claims were traced limitation by limitation: rigid base with first/second sides, motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid low-friction perimeter member at the perimeter of the second side terminating in an end bearing face, the non-sealing clearance admitting ambient air, the volumetric extraction rate maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, the resulting holding force replacing operator downforce, the all-rigid vibration transmission path free of elastomer/foam/resilient mount, and slidability under a maintained differential all trace to the disclosure paragraphs on the rigid loop or skirt, "not intended to form a complete airtight seal", "continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter", "holds the device firmly against the tile without requiring the operator to press downward", "connected to the tile through rigid components", and "allows the device to slide freely across different areas of the tile"; dependent limitations (closed loop, plastic/metal/PTFE/combination, free of rubber-elastomer-foam, holding force without operator downforce, continuous extraction, vacuum pump, handle for guiding, flexible pulling element of rope/wire/cable, decoupled-control whereby clause, and stirring elements) each trace to an exact disclosure or USER sentence; claim 10/20 and the FIG. 6 embodiment trace to the autonomous-mode USER passage. All seventeen numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked for one-to-one meaning across the numeral table, detailed description, and all six figure briefs; each numeral is defined once, used consistently, and appears on at least one sheet, and every brief's identification list matches its "Numerals appearing on this figure" and bullet lists exactly. All six figure briefs and the corresponding Brief Description entries were compared: FIG. 1 (10, 12, 18, 20, 24, 36, 44), FIG. 2 (12, 14, 20, 22, 24, 36), FIG. 3 (16, 24), FIG. 4 (24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42), FIG. 5 (10, 24, 36, 46), FIG. 6 (10, 48) — each numeral set is covered by the matching paragraph of draft/07-drawings.md, including the FIG. 2 enumeration of sectioned versus elevation bodies and the FIG. 6 single-body recital. Section-line designations are repeated identically in every place they occur: line 2-2 appears in the FIG. 3 brief (horizontal line, numeral 2 at each end), the FIG. 2 brief view line, the FIG. 2 drawing description, and the detailed description; line 4-4 appears in the FIG. 3 brief (vertical line, numeral 4 at each end), the FIG. 4 brief view line, the FIG. 4 drawing description, and the detailed description. Functional-surface geometry was reviewed under the strict rule: the briefs make no statement about taper, angle, runout direction, deeper end, radial or circumferential end position, or contact extent — FIG. 4 expressly disclaims the flat form of the bearing-face end and asserts "no extent of contact", FIG. 3 disclaims frame width, plan form, and the angular position at which each section line crosses the ring, FIG. 1 disclaims block order, spacing and handle mounting arrangement, FIG. 2 disclaims the port form of the unhatched passage, and FIG. 6 disclaims number, form, placement and any engagement beneath. The residual depicted relationships (perimeter member flush at the base perimeter, band standing on the tile, base-to-tile non-contact, layer stack of covering element on bonding material on substrate, and fluid communication through the base) each trace to affirmative disclosure sentences. Every depiction convention stays confined to the figure briefs; no "by way of example", "any closed outline", or renderer-justifying broadening appears in the title, field, background, summary, drawing description, detailed description, claims or abstract, and no word such as "rectangular" leaks into the shape-neutral application text. Background prior-art characterizations were treated as exempt from inventor support. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains in any draft section, claim/dependency numbering is well formed (three independent claims, twenty total, all dependencies proper), terminology is uniform between claims and description, and the abstract is single-paragraph and under 150 words. No unsupported technical assertion or verified internal inconsistency was found.

content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, tracing each claim limitation, numbered part, and figure statement to the disclosure and the USER passages.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. Every limitation of claims 1-20 (rigid base with first/second sides, motor coupled to the first side, perimeter member extending at the perimeter of the second side and surrounding the chamber, low-friction rigid material list, end-face bearing face, clearance along at least part of the member with ambient air entering, extraction rate sufficient to hold the chamber below atmospheric while air keeps entering, all-rigid vibration path with no elastomeric/foam/resilient member, slidability under maintained differential, closed loop, vacuum pump, continuous running, handle, flexible pulling element and rope/wire/cable species, decoupled-control system whereby clause, stirring elements, and the four method steps) traces to the disclosure ("vibration motor coupled to a first side of a rigid base", "air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump ... in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side", "rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material such as plastic, metal, PTFE", "not intended to form a complete airtight seal ... restricts airflow into the chamber while maintaining rigid contact with the tile", "continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter", "holds the device firmly against the tile without requiring the operator to press downward", "slide freely across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact", "one or more handles used primarily for guiding", "rope, wire, cable, or similar flexible pulling element") and, for the autonomous third embodiment and the Field's "autonomously moving", to the USER passage "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion". All seventeen numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked for single meaning and for use across the description and briefs; each brief's identification bullets match its declared numeral list, and 24, 36 and 10 hold one referent across FIGS. 1-6. All six figure briefs and the six paragraphs of the Brief Description of the Drawings were compared item by item: omissions (motor/handle in FIG. 2; motor/pump in FIG. 5; separate parts and covering element in FIG. 6), sectioned bodies in FIG. 2, and the FIG. 4 layer stack agree. Section designations 2-2 and 4-4 are used identically in the source-view brief (FIG. 3), the resulting-view briefs (FIGS. 2 and 4), and the drawing description. Generic outlines (slab, band, ring, blocks, column, closed cord path), hatching directions, block order, ring width, section-line angular position, the flat lower end of the perimeter column, the FIG. 2 communication gap, and the number/position of the stirring elements are each confined to their briefs and expressly marked as depiction conventions, with no taper, angle, deeper-end, runout, or contact-topology statement verbalized, so they were not reported. Two items are reported: an application-text sentence that carries a drawing convention out of the figure brief and conflicts with the definite section-line recitals in the Brief Description, and a small claim-support gap where the stirring elements of claim 10 are recited without the source's stated link to the vibration-driven forward motion. No placeholder, drafting note, question, instruction, or unresolved alternative remains in any section, and the abstract is 145 words.

findings.title: Drawing convention about section-line placement leaked into the application text and contradicts the Brief Description
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "The perimeter member and the chamber", final sentence of the clearance paragraph (cf. draft/07-drawings.md, FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 paragraphs; figures/FIG-3 brief)
findings.detail: The detailed description states: "The section lines 2-2 and 4-4 in FIG. 3 are schematic indicators of where such sections may be taken." That sentence exists only to justify the renderer's arbitrary choice of where the two section lines cross the ring, a choice the FIG. 3 brief already confines to itself ("Their drawn positions, including the angular position at which each crosses the ring, are a placement convention for this sheet only."). A depiction convention must stay inside the figure brief; verbalizing it in the application adds an unsupported statement about the drawings, and no inventor passage says anything about where sections are taken. It also conflicts with the definite recitals in the Brief Description of the Drawings, which state that FIG. 2 "is a vertical sectional view taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 3" and FIG. 4 "is an enlarged fragmentary sectional view taken on line 4-4 of FIG. 3" — a section line identifies where a section is taken, not merely where one "may be taken". The nearest source passages, "the rigid perimeter is not intended to form a complete airtight seal" and "continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter", support the clearance itself but say nothing about section positions.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The section lines 2-2 and 4-4 in FIG. 3 are schematic indicators of where such sections may be taken." (draft/08-detailed-description.md). Conflicting candidate text: "FIG. 2 is a vertical sectional view taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 3" and "FIG. 4 is an enlarged fragmentary sectional view taken on line 4-4 of FIG. 3, at a place along the perimeter member where the clearance is present" (draft/07-drawings.md). Nearest inventor passage, showing the gap: "Unlike conventional vacuum grippers or suction cups, the rigid perimeter is not intended to form a complete airtight seal" (input/disclosure.md) — no statement about sections or their placement.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence "The section lines 2-2 and 4-4 in FIG. 3 are schematic indicators of where such sections may be taken." from draft/08-detailed-description.md. The paragraph then runs "... FIG. 4 is an enlarged fragmentary sectional view showing the clearance 34 that is present along at least part of the perimeter member 24. The enlarged detail of FIG. 4 also shows ...", which remains coherent, and the placement convention stays where it belongs, in the FIG. 3 brief. Change nothing in the figure briefs or the Brief Description.

findings.title: Claim 10's stirring elements are recited in the description without the source's stated link to the vibration-driven forward motion
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "Embodiment with stirring elements"; draft/09-claims.md, claim 10
findings.detail: Claim 10 recites "one or more stirring elements carried by the vibration device", but the description introduces the stirring elements 48 and then attributes the autonomous motion to the vibration alone, so the claimed element is left with no described function: "The vibration device 10 carries one or more stirring elements 48. The vibration produced by the vibration motor 18 may cause a constant forward motion of the vibration device 10 ...". The inventor's own passage supplies the missing link and is the only authority for this embodiment: "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion". Restoring that link is source-faithful and adds no matter beyond the USER passage; it does not assert any location, form, count, or engagement with the covering element, all of which the sources leave open and which the FIG. 6 brief correctly disclaims.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The vibration device 10 carries one or more stirring elements 48. The vibration produced by the vibration motor 18 may cause a constant forward motion of the vibration device 10, so that the vibration device 10 need not be pulled or guided by hand ..." (draft/08-detailed-description.md). Claim: "10. The vibration device of claim 1, further comprising one or more stirring elements carried by the vibration device." Inventor passage: "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion" (input/conversation.md, USER).
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md, replace "The vibration produced by the vibration motor 18 may cause a constant forward motion of the vibration device 10" with "The vibration produced by the vibration motor 18, acting through the one or more stirring elements 48, may cause a constant forward motion of the vibration device 10". Leave the remainder of the sentence, claim 10, claim 20, the numeral table, and the FIG. 6 brief unchanged.

A depiction convention must stay inside the figure brief; verbalizing it in the application adds an unsupported statement about the drawings, and no inventor passage says anything about where sections are taken. It also conflicts with the definite recitals in the Brief Description of the Drawings, which state that FIG. 2 "is a vertical sectional view taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 3" and FIG. 4 "is an enlarged fragmentary sectional view taken on line 4-4 of FIG. 3" — a section line identifies where a section is taken, not merely where one "may be taken". The nearest source passages, "the rigid perimeter is not intended to form a complete airtight seal" and "continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter", support the clearance itself but say nothing about section positions.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The section lines 2-2 and 4-4 in FIG. 3 are schematic indicators of where such sections may be taken." (draft/08-detailed-description.md). Conflicting candidate text: "FIG. 2 is a vertical sectional view taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 3" and "FIG. 4 is an enlarged fragmentary sectional view taken on line 4-4 of FIG. 3, at a place along the perimeter member where the clearance is present" (draft/07-drawings.md). Nearest inventor passage, showing the gap: "Unlike conventional vacuum grippers or suction cups, the rigid perimeter is not intended to form a complete airtight seal" (input/disclosure.md) — no statement about sections or their placement.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence "The section lines 2-2 and 4-4 in FIG. 3 are schematic indicators of where such sections may be taken." from draft/08-detailed-description.md. The paragraph then runs "... FIG. 4 is an enlarged fragmentary sectional view showing the clearance 34 that is present along at least part of the perimeter member 24. The enlarged detail of FIG. 4 also shows ...", which remains coherent, and the placement convention stays where it belongs, in the FIG. 3 brief. Change nothing in the figure briefs or the Brief Description.

findings.title: Claim 10's stirring elements are recited in the description without the source's stated link to the vibration-driven forward motion
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "Embodiment with stirring elements"; draft/09-claims.md, claim 10
findings.detail: Claim 10 recites "one or more stirring elements carried by the vibration device", but the description introduces the stirring elements 48 and then attributes the autonomous motion to the vibration alone, so the claimed element is left with no described function: "The vibration device 10 carries one or more stirring elements 48. The vibration produced by the vibration motor 18 may cause a constant forward motion of the vibration device 10 ...". The inventor's own passage supplies the missing link and is the only authority for this embodiment: "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion". Restoring that link is source-faithful and adds no matter beyond the USER passage; it does not assert any location, form, count, or engagement with the covering element, all of which the sources leave open and which the FIG. 6 brief correctly disclaims.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The vibration device 10 carries one or more stirring elements 48. findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md, replace "The vibration produced by the vibration motor 18 may cause a constant forward motion of the vibration device 10" with "The vibration produced by the vibration motor 18, acting through the one or more stirring elements 48, may cause a constant forward motion of the vibration device 10". Leave the remainder of the sentence, claim 10, claim 20, the numeral table, and the FIG. 6 brief unchanged.
